question.text: Two elements $A$ and $B$ have similar chemical properties. They don't form solid hydrogencarbonates, but react with nitrogen to form nitrides. A and B, respectively, are :
Which of the following has minimum melting point?

solution.text:
Ionic compounds have high melting point. Greater the ionic character, more is melting point. $\mathrm{HCl}$ has least ionic character because of maximum electronegativity difference between the two constituent elements, ( $\mathrm{H}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ ) among $\mathrm{CsF}, \mathrm{HCl}, \mathrm{HF}$ and $\mathrm{LiF}$

$\therefore \mathrm{HCl}$ has minimum melting point.

question.text: The correct order of mobility of alkali metal ions in aqueous solution is-

solution.text:
Mobility of alkali ions in aqueous solution ∝1 size of hydrated ion 

The mobility of alkali ions is inversely proportional to the size of ion in hydrated state, because bigger ion can't move faster. Also, small ion get hydrolysed to large exent due to which its size get increased. In other words, smaller ion will form hydrated ion of larger size.

Hence, correct order of mobility is

Rb+>K+>Na+>Li+

question.text: Sodium sulphate is soluble in water but barium sulphate is insoluble because

options.text: hydration energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is more than of its lattice energy
lattice energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>BaSO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> is more than its hydration energy

solution.text:
For any solution to become soluble in water hydration energy of the solution should me more than its lattice energy. Here the hydration energy of sodium sulphate is more than lattice energy but in case of barium sulphate lattice energy of barium sulphate is more than its hydration energy.  

For dissolution hydration energy must be more higher (-ve) value than of lattice energy. Thus, (c) is the correct answer.

question.text: The alkali metals form salt-like hydrides by the direct synthesis at elevated temperature. The thermal stability of these hydrides decreases in which of the following orders?

solution.text: The stability of alkali metal hydrides decreases from Li to Cs. It is due to the fact that $\mathrm{M}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds becomes weaker with increase in size of alkali metals as we move down the group from $\mathrm{Li}$ to $\mathrm{Cs}$. Thus the order of stability of hydrides is $\mathrm{LiH}>\mathrm{NaH}>\mathrm{KH}>\mathrm{RbH}>\mathrm{CsH}$

question.text: Which of the following salt would give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> with hot and dil <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>SO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> and also decolourises <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Br</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> water?

solution.text:
When Na2SO3 reacts with hot and dil H2SO4, it gives SO2g which decolourises bromine-water.

The reaction proceed as follows:

(i) Na2SO3+H2SO4⟶Na2SO4+SO2+H2O

(ii) Br2+H2O⟶2HBr+O

(iii) SO2+O⟶SO3 (decolourisation of bromine-water)

question.text: Which of the following property of alkaline earth metal increases with their atomic number?

options.text: solubility of their hydroxides in water
solubility of their sulphate in water

solution.text: The lattice energy of the hydroxides of alkaline earth metal decreases more rapidly than their hydration energy leading to more negative value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ΔH</mi><mtext>sol</mtext></msub></math> down the group. More negative is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ΔH</mi><mtext>sol</mtext></msub></math>, more is the solubility of compounds. Hence the solubility of hydroxides of alkaline earth metal increases with their atomic number.

question.text: Which of the following elements mostly form covalent compounds?

solution.text:
First member of 1st group i.e. lithium, mostly form covalent compounds due to its small size and comparatively high I.E. (with respect to other members of its group). 

Covalent character depends upon the atomic radii. Smaller the atomic radii, more the covalent character i.e. the covalent character is inversely proportional to atomic radii.

question.text: Which of the following compounds is thermodynamically is the most stable?

solution.text:
The thermal stability of carbonates increases down the group. So, the order of thermal stability of carbonates of alkaline earth metals is
$$
\mathrm{BaCO}_3>\mathrm{CaCO}_3>\mathrm{MgCO}_3>\mathrm{BeCO}_3 .
$$
Therefore, $\mathrm{BaCO}_3$ is thermodynamically most stable and $\mathrm{BeCO}_3$ is least stable.
